column4: Visit note | 2025-08-04 12:30 PM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Hafiz Bhuiyan, 24, male. Mr. Bhuiyan presents saying he needs to lie in a dark room because bright light hurts his eyes during attacks. He works as a mobile phone repair technician, and his symptoms have been worse since bright screens at a new job in Rampura. He experiences about 4 headache days a month. He has Essential hypertension. He denies weakness, numbness, or visual loss. On examination: BP 143/90 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 58 kg. Neurological examination is normal. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-08-04 04:00 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Tuhin Islam, 70, male. Mr. Islam reports that his symptoms are worse at night, with burning in both feet and numbness in his toes. He is a retired civil servant and notes his discomfort has been worse since walking barefoot at home in Old Dhaka. He has no reported comorbidity. He denies skin breaks, ulcers, or shooting limb pains. On examination: reduced sensation at 4 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 129/76 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 55 kg. Peripheral pulses are palpable. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to check his feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep his blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-08-05 04:30 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Jesmin Akter, 31, female. Mrs. Akter complains of brittle nails, getting breathless on the stairs, and constant tiredness, along with a craving to chew ice and a sore smooth tongue with little tiredness. She works as a construction worker and her complaints started after a stomach illness during a stay in Noakhali. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies chest pain or severe dizziness. On examination: haemoglobin 9.7 g/dL, BP 121/85 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 69 kg. Conjunctivae appear pale. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: referral to Gastroenterology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up after the Gastroenterology review.

Visit note | 2025-08-06 10:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Mostafa Dewan, 79, male. Mr. Dewan attended after seeing a high reading on a pharmacy machine, alongside occasional dizziness, and no other complaints. He is a retired civil servant and noticed this after a stressful month of overtime in Mymensingh. He has no reported comorbidity. He denies chest tightness, shortness of breath, or blackouts. On examination: BP 154/105 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 62 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no added sounds. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: referral to Endocrinology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check his blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up after the Endocrinology review.

Visit note | 2025-08-09 11:30 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Taslima Bepari, 65, female. Mrs. Bepari attends for review and reports weight gain and dry skin. She works as a shopkeeper and her symptoms were noticed by colleagues in Faridpur who remarked on weight gain. She has Essential hypertension. She reports taking her regular treatments and denies tremor, palpitations, or heat intolerance. On examination: TSH 9.0 mIU/L, BP 146/93 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 72 kg. Skin is dry and reflexes show delayed relaxation. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: chronic follow-up: continue current medicines, no new prescription issued; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.
